evals.prompt: Audit our Rust workspace for hidden trade-offs between compile time and runtime performance
evals.expected_output: Runs TRIZ contradiction audit, identifies specific crates/files, maps to principles #13 #35, writes report to analysis/triz-<scope>-YYYY-MM-DD.md
assertions: Output names a target scope (crates/, scripts/, or specific crate)
Contradiction stated explicitly: 'improving [X] causes [Y] to worsen'
Maps contradiction to specific TRIZ principle number
Suggests a Rust-idiomatic resolution pattern (feature flag, dyn dispatch, cargo-bloat, etc.)

evals.prompt: Run a TRIZ audit on scripts/ to find workflow contradictions
evals.expected_output: Performs SCOPE SCAN on scripts/, identifies contradictions, maps to principles, writes analysis/triz-scripts-YYYY-MM-DD.md
assertions: Scans scripts/ directory for pain points
Each contradiction mapped to a TRIZ principle
Report file path follows analysis/triz-scripts-YYYY-MM-DD.md convention

evals.prompt: Find innovation opportunities in our tokio-based async architecture using TRIZ
evals.expected_output: Audits async architecture, identifies contradictions like async surface vs blocking cost, maps to #1 #15, proposes feature gates or spawn_blocking pattern
assertions: Identifies at least one async-specific contradiction

evals.prompt: I think our Cargo.toml workspace is over-engineered but I can't see why. Can you TRIZ audit it?
evals.expected_output: Audits Cargo.toml workspace, identifies complexity vs functionality contradiction, maps to #1 #9 #15, suggests workspace inheritance or feature segmentation
assertions: States contradiction in the form 'improving X worsens Y'
References specific Cargo.toml patterns (workspace.package, features, dependencies)
Proposes a concrete refactor (e.g., workspace inheritance)

evals.prompt: Our CI takes 25 minutes. Find the contradictions in .github/workflows/
evals.expected_output: Audits CI workflows, identifies build matrix vs CI minutes contradiction, maps to #1 #9, proposes cargo-hack and sharding
assertions: Contradiction: build matrix (improve) vs CI minutes (worsen)
References cargo-hack or workspace test sharding

evals.prompt: Do a swarm-based TRIZ audit on crates/ — different agents per crate
evals.expected_output: Orchestrates parallel TRIZ analysis across crates, integrates findings into single report, uses agent-coordination principles
assertions: Mentions parallel or swarm execution across crates
Output aggregates per-crate contradictions into one analysis/ file
Identifies at least one cross-crate contradiction

evals.prompt: Our trait has too many methods and downstream users are complaining about compile time. TRIZ this
evals.expected_output: Identifies API surface vs compile time contradiction, maps to #2 #6, suggests taking out (#2) into smaller traits or sealed traits (#6)
assertions: Contradiction stated: API surface (improve) vs compile time (worsen)
References trait methods or sealed traits
Proposes splitting trait or using sealed pattern

evals.prompt: We're forced to add unsafe to bypass the borrow checker. Use TRIZ to find a safe design
evals.expected_output: Audits unsafe usage, identifies lifetime or ownership contradiction, maps to #7 (Nesting) or #17 (Another dimension), proposes Cow, newtype, or wrapper
assertions: Contradiction: borrow safety (improve) vs API flexibility (worsen)
References Rust-specific patterns: Cow, newtype, PhantomData, lifetime generics

evals.prompt: Contradiction audit on .agents/ — find trade-offs in our skill index generator

assertions: Suggests a separation or restructuring pattern

evals.prompt: We have 50+ features in Cargo.toml and binary is huge. Find the contradiction
